observation_summary: The type inference engine fails to correctly infer the type of an anonymous object when it is part of a union type in a function parameter, resulting in an empty object type instead of the expected record type.
reasoning_summary: The issue is a failure in the type inference logic (a computational procedure) when handling union types containing record types. This is a procedural error in how the compiler calculates the resulting type, which is a classic Algorithm/Method defect. It is not a missing guard (Checking), a simple initialization error (Assignment/Initialization), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object).
evidence_used: Bug report description: anonymous object type inference inconsistency when used in union
evidence_gaps: The specific source code file responsible for the type inference logic (e.g., TypeInference.java) was not provided in the snippets, though the test failure clearly points to a logic error in the inference algorithm.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The capability to infer types exists, but the specific logic for union types is flawed, which is an algorithmic issue rather than a missing design capability.
While it involves the relationship between union types and record types, the root cause is the procedural logic used to resolve these types during inference.
